memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "One beka per person, that is, half a shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, from everyone who had crossed over to those counted, twenty years old or more, a total of 603,550 men." - Exod 38:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Every man paid exactly the same. Half a shekel. Not scaled to income, status, tribe or age.

The earlier instruction made this explicit: the rich were not to give more and the poor were not to give less (Exod 30:15). This was redemption money, and redemption cost the same for everybody.

Sit with what that means. The wealthiest man in Israel could not purchase a better standing before God. The poorest could not be excluded for lack of funds.

That is the gospel's logic exactly. All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and all are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus (Rom 3:23-24). Same problem, same price, same remedy.

Our world does not work this way. Better lawyers, better healthcare, better opportunities are all available at a price. It is easy to assume God operates on the same principles.

He does not. There is no premium tier in the kingdom of God. No one gets closer to the Father because of what they can pay, and no one is turned away for being unable to pay.

And note the final figure: 603,550 men, each individually counted. Not a crowd. A number made of names.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you unconsciously think some people are more acceptable to God than others?
2. Have you tried to earn standing with God that Christ already purchased?
3. How does this shape the way you treat people of different backgrounds?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that the price was the same for all and that Christ paid it. Let me never look down on anyone You have redeemed. Amen.
